## Findings — MP-04.b Pages Adapter Review

**Scope reviewed:** `scripts/build-pages-spike.mjs`, `scripts/test-pages-spike.mjs`, `spikes/pages/{wrangler.jsonc,_headers,_routes.json,README.md,functions/api/[[path]].ts}`, `tests/unit/pages-spike.test.ts`. Per orchestration policy this is a bounded Sonnet/medium read-only pass.

### Verified — sound
1. **Source isolation (build script):** Uses `git ls-files` (tracked-only) plus an explicit allowlist (`src/`, `public/`, 4 root config files) and blocks `src/app/api/**`, `src/middleware.ts`, and any `.env*` basename before copying (`build-pages-spike.mjs:48-56`). Copies land only in a per-run stage dir under `build/pages-spike`; `next.config.ts` (export mode) is written only into that copy (line 64), never to root. Protected-path hashes are computed via read-only `readFile` of the original root files (lines 71-73) — no write path touches them. `insideArtifact()` guards the only two writes outside the stage (`publicOutput`, `manifest.json`) to stay under `artifactRoot` (lines 15-18, 89-101). No defect found; satisfies check (1).
2. **Cleanup scope (test script):** Only kills `child.pid`, the process it itself spawned (`taskkill /pid <own pid>` on win32, else `SIGTERM`) — lines 66-71. No broader process/session kill. Satisfies (2).
3. **Function semantics:** `[[path]].ts` returns 200 GET/HEAD with `readiness:false`, `database`/`auth: "not-configured"`; HEAD strips body (lines 11-16, 32-38). Unsupported methods on health → 405 + `Allow: GET, HEAD` (26-30). All other paths (incl. `/api/sync`) → 503, and the 503 handler never echoes request body, so it cannot fake-ACK a queued sale (41-44) — this matches CLAUDE.md's "never drop/fake-ack a queued sale" concern at the boundary of this fixture. Every response sets no-store + nosniff + frame/referrer/permissions headers unconditionally (1-8). `_routes.json` scopes Functions to `/api/*` only, so `_headers`' static no-store doesn't need to (and per README correctly doesn't claim to) secure Function responses. Satisfies (3).
4. **Test reality:** `test-pages-spike.mjs` reserves a real ephemeral port, spawns the actual `wrangler pages dev` binary against the built output, polls a genuine HTTP health check with a 30s deadline before asserting (36-43), and every assertion is a real `fetch` + `assert()` that throws (nonzero exit) on failure — including on a missing/failed artifact, since a missing `output` dir will make wrangler fail to serve and `ready()` will time out and throw. The unit test (`tests/unit/pages-spike.test.ts`) exercises the exported handler directly with real `Request`/`Response` objects and checks status/headers/body, not just truthiness. Neither script claims hydrated UI or auth proof; README explicitly disclaims that. Satisfies (4), with one caveat below.

### Concrete defect
**Inconsistent secret scrubbing between build and test scripts.** `build-pages-spike.mjs` deliberately scrubs env via `withoutSecrets()` before running `next build` (line 76). `test-pages-spike.mjs` does **not** do this: it spawns `wrangler pages dev` with `{ ...process.env, CI: '1', NO_PROXY: ..., WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS: 'false' }` (lines 23-26), passing the full ambient environment — including any `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`/`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`/other credentials that may be set on the developer machine — into the wrangler process. `wrangler.jsonc` has no `account_id` and no `pages deploy` command is ever invoked, so this does not itself prove remote/account access occurs. But it is a real inconsistency with the project's own stated secret-isolation intent and an unnecessary exposure surface for the local emulator step. **Recommend:** apply the same `withoutSecrets()`-style allowlist to the wrangler child's env in the test script.

### Not verified (unperformed, out of scope for read-only review)
Whether `wrangler pages dev` makes any outbound network call in this installed version (e.g., version-check telemetry despite `WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false`) was not executed/observed — flagged as hypothesis only, not confirmed. No claim of full G1 or production safety is made.
